How does turmeric paper help identify a base?
questions.a: Turmeric stain stays yellow in acid but turns reddish-brown with a base, so it acts as an indicator.

questions.q: Name two olfactory indicators and what they show.
questions.a: Onion and vanilla essence lose their characteristic smell in a base; the smell change signals a basic solution.

questions.q: What colour does litmus show in acids and in bases?
questions.a: Blue litmus turns red in an acid and red litmus turns blue in a base.

concepts.title: Reaction of Metals with Acids and Bases

questions.q: What gas is released when a metal reacts with an acid, and how is it tested?
questions.a: Hydrogen gas; it burns with a pop sound when a burning splinter is brought near.

questions.q: Do all metals react with bases? What forms when zinc reacts with sodium hydroxide?
questions.a: Only some reactive amphoteric metals like zinc and aluminium; zinc gives sodium zincate with hydrogen gas.

questions.q: Complete: Metal carbonate + acid gives?
questions.a: Salt + water + carbon dioxide - effervescence of CO2 is seen.

concepts.title: Reaction of Acids with Carbonates and Hydrogencarbonates

questions.q: What happens when baking soda is treated with vinegar?
questions.a: Sodium hydrogencarbonate reacts with the acid to give salt, water and brisk effervescence of carbon dioxide.

questions.q: How is carbon dioxide gas identified in a reaction?
questions.a: By passing it through lime water, which turns milky due to calcium carbonate formed.

questions.q: Why do metal hydrogencarbonates also give CO2 with acids?
questions.a: They contain the hydrogencarbonate ion, which acids convert to water and carbon dioxide along with a salt.

concepts.title: Oxide Reactions and Their Chemical Nature

questions.q: What happens when a metal oxide reacts with an acid?
questions.a: Metal oxides are basic: with an acid they form salt and water, e.g. copper oxide with dilute HCl gives copper chloride and water.

questions.q: Why are metal oxides called basic oxides?
questions.a: Because they neutralise acids forming salt and water, the hallmark of bases.

questions.q: Name one oxide that reacts both with acids and bases.
questions.a: Aluminium oxide is amphoteric - it reacts with acids to give salt and water and also with strong bases to give a salt.

concepts.title: Ionization of Acids and Bases in Water

questions.q: What is formed when HCl dissolves in water?
questions.a: Hydrogen ions join water molecules giving hydronium ions (H3O+) along with chloride ions.

questions.q: Why does a dry HCl gas sample not turn litmus red?
questions.a: Without water, HCl cannot ionise to give H+(aq) ions, and only ions show acidic behaviour.

questions.q: What do acids and bases produce in aqueous solutions?
questions.a: Acids give H3O+ (hydronium) ions and bases give OH- (hydroxide) ions in water.

questions.q: A sample of hydrochloric acid tests at pH 1 while a weak acid sample tests at pH 4. How many times higher is the hydrogen ion concentration of the pH 1 sample?
questions.a: 1000 times

questions.q: A soft drink has pH 2 and tomato juice has pH 4. How many times greater is the drink's hydrogen ion concentration?
questions.a: 100 times

questions.q: A lemon juice sample of pH 3 is compared with tomato juice of pH 4. How many times more concentrated in H+ ions is the lemon juice?
questions.a: 10 times

questions.q: Gastric juice has pH about 1 while saliva is nearly neutral at pH 6. How many times stronger is the gastric juice in H+ ions?
questions.a: 100000 times

questions.q: Two soil samples test at pH 5 and pH 7. How many times greater is the hydrogen ion concentration of the more acidic sample?
questions.a: 100 times

concepts.title: Importance of pH in Everyday Life

questions.q: Why is the pH of the mouth kept below 7.8 for healthy teeth?
questions.a: Tooth enamel decays when mouth pH falls below about 5.5; keeping pH near neutral prevents acid attack by bacteria.

questions.q: How does an antacid cure indigestion?
questions.a: It is a mild base (like milk of magnesia) that neutralises excess hydrochloric acid in the stomach.

questions.q: What is the use of treating soil with quicklime or slaked lime?
questions.a: When soil turns too acidic for crops, farmers mix in bases like lime to neutralise the acidity; slaked lime also treats acidic factory waste.

concepts.title: Classification and pH Nature of Salts

questions.q: What kind of salt is formed by a strong acid and a strong base?
questions.a: A neutral salt (pH 7), e.g. sodium chloride from HCl and NaOH.

questions.q: Why is washing soda solution basic while that of aluminium chloride acidic?
questions.a: Washing soda comes from a strong base and weak acid, so its solution is basic; aluminium chloride comes from a strong acid and weak base, so its solution is acidic.

questions.q: What pH would you expect for ammonium chloride solution?
questions.a: Below 7 - it is a salt of a strong acid and weak base, so its solution is acidic.

concepts.title: Industrial Chemicals Derived from Common Salt

questions.q: What is the chlor-alkali process and what does it yield?
questions.a: Electrolysis of brine: at the cathode hydrogen is released, at the anode chlorine, and sodium hydroxide forms in solution.

questions.q: Name three important products of the chlor-alkali process and one use of each.
questions.a: Sodium hydroxide (soaps), chlorine (bleaching powder, PVC), hydrogen (fuels, margarine, fertilisers).

questions.q: What is bleaching powder and how is it made?
questions.a: Calcium oxychloride, made by passing chlorine gas over dry slaked lime; used to bleach cotton and disinfect water.

concepts.title: Water of Crystallisation and Plaster of Paris

questions.q: What is water of crystallisation?
questions.a: Fixed number of water molecules present in one formula unit of a salt, e.g. copper sulphate crystals hold five waters.

questions.q: What happens when blue copper sulphate crystals are heated?
questions.a: They lose water of crystallisation, turn white; on adding water the blue colour returns.

questions.q: How is plaster of Paris obtained from gypsum?
questions.a: Gypsum (CaSO4.2H2O) is heated to 373 K, losing water to give plaster of Paris CaSO4.1/2H2O, which sets to a hard mass with water.
